chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn Suqah, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mundhir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man comes to me seeking the 'inah [buy-back], so I buy the goods for him with a profit margin, then I sell them to him, then I buy them back from him in my place.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he has the option, if he wishes he sells, and if he wishes he does not sell, and you also have the option: if you wish you buy, and if you wish you do not buy, so there is no problem.'

He (the narrator) said: 'I said: 'But the people of the Masjid allege that this is invalid, and they say that if he brings it back after some months, it would be correct.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is preceding and delaying, so there is no problem with it.'

key_terms.الْعِينَةَ: Inah: A buy-back transaction used to simulate interest-based lending.
key_terms.بِالْخِيَارِ: Bi-al-khiyar: Having the option/choice to accept or reject the deal.
key_terms.تَقْدِيمٌ وَ تَأْخِيرٌ: Ta'dim wa ta'khir: Preceding and delaying; referring to the timing of the buy-back.
key_terms.مُرَابَحَةً: Murabahah: A sale with a known profit margin.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on 'inah (buy-back) transactions in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith validates the 'inah (buy-back) transaction as a permissible mechanism for simulating interest-free loans, a critical issue in Shia commercial jurisprudence. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the validity hinges on the mutual option of cancellation (khiyar) at each stage, thereby refuting the view that a temporal delay of months is a strict condition for the transaction's integrity. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia fiqh in adapting commercial practices to practical economic needs while maintaining contractual validity.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Sowqat, from Al Husayn Bin Al Munzar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man comes over to me seeking the buy-back (الْعِينَةَ). So I buy the goods (from someone else) for him with a profit, then I sell these to him, then I buy these back from him in my place (instantly – takin back the returned goods)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When he was with the choice, if he so desires to he sells or if he so desires to he does not sell, and you as well were with the choice, if you so desire to you buy, and if you so desire to you do not buy, so there is no problem’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘But the people of the Masjid are alleging that this is invalid, and they are saying that if he comes with it after some months, it would be correct’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is preceding and delaying, so there is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn Suwqah from al- Husayn ibn al-Mundhir who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘A man comes to me and asks for ‘Aynah. I then buy for him the merchandise in the manner of Murabahah (capital plus profit) then sell it to him, then buy it from him at the same place. He (the Imam) said, Tf he has the choice to sell if he likes or not to sell and you also have the choice to buy if you like or do not buy if you do not like, it is not unlawful.’

I then said, ‘People of the Masjid think it is not valid. They say, “If he brings it after few months it is valid.’” He (the Imam) said, ‘This is making early what is later and late what is early and it is not unlawful.’”
